notes: RBox revision of symmetry: flips a property that holds (bordering is mutual) to its opposite. Symmetry of 'borders' follows from no other tag, so the revision has no premise route back. Migrated 2026-11-11 to the new layout. Audit fixes: the bare question "Is the relation 'borders' asymmetric?" was answered yes by 3 of 4 models, a reading problem with the word 'asymmetric' rather than a gap in what they hold (every model answers the instances by symmetry), so the direct question and the propositional statement now say what asymmetry means ("only ever holds in one direction between two places"). The Danube side fact was missed by 3 models and is replaced by Paris. Instances follow examples/geography-replace-0904: minor, true pairs (Rutland and Leicestershire, Monmouthshire and Herefordshire) instead of France and Spain or Brazil and Argentina, whose converses are famous stored facts a model could answer from against the edited property. Yes and no are balanced by phrasing: the first instance asks whether the fact rules out the converse (no, then yes; the cross-lingual queries ask it), the second whether the converse follows (yes, then no). zh uses the county names 拉特兰郡 and 莱斯特郡. Near asks the same property of another symmetric geography relation (a leak would turn its no into yes); far asks a different property of an unrelated relation. hops counts the instance fact in the prompt as the bridge (1 + 1), as the other RBox records do. Locality references are the logical answers; the scoring gold is the model's own pre-edit answer.
